transcript.content: Hello, welcome. What brings you in to see me today?

I feel like I’ve lost the drive and interest in everything I used to care about, even my students and the arts stuff I loved. My husband and a close coworker noticed how much I've been pulling away and encouraged me to seek help because it's starting to seriously affect my teaching career. I just feel like the spark I used to have has completely gone out.
Have you ever experienced periods lasting at least a few days where you felt the exact opposite—unusually energetic, active, or needing very little sleep?
No, I've never had periods like that where I felt unusually energetic or hyperactive. If anything, it's been the exact opposite—I just feel completely drained and have no drive at all.
How long have you been feeling this way? Has this lack of drive and interest been going on continuously for at least two years, or is it a more recent change?

It hasn't been two years, but it has been going on for a little over a year now, about fourteen months. It started building around the time the new curriculum was rolled out at school. Since then, I've just gradually pulled away from everything.
Is this the first time in your life you've experienced a period of depression and loss of interest like this, or have you had similar episodes in the past that eventually got better?

Yes, this is the first time I've ever experienced anything like this. I have always managed my teaching, coaching, and theater responsibilities really well until this past year. It's completely new and overwhelming for me.
Along with the loss of drive and interest, have you also been feeling consistently sad, down, or empty most of the day?

I wouldn't say I feel particularly sad or down, to be honest. It's more that I just feel completely flat and empty of any drive. The spark is just gone, and I can't find the motivation to care about anything anymore.
Have you noticed any changes in your sleep patterns, appetite, or physical energy levels since these feelings started?

I haven't really noticed any significant changes in my sleep or my appetite. But my physical energy feels extremely low, and I usually just end up sitting on the couch after work because I lack the motivation to do anything at all.
Have you been experiencing any feelings of worthlessness or excessive, inappropriate guilt during this past year?

No, I haven't really experienced feelings of worthlessness or guilt. It is more of a profound lack of drive, motivation, and interest in my life. I just feel completely empty of the spark I used to have.
Have you noticed any difficulty concentrating, focusing on your teaching tasks, or making decisions since these changes began?

Yes, I've had a lot of trouble focusing, to the point where I'll suddenly stop mid-lesson and just stand there staring at the whiteboard or fiddling with papers while my students sit there confused. I've also been missing deadlines for curriculum planning because it's just so hard to stay on task. It feels like I completely lose track of what I'm doing.
Since these changes began, have you had any thoughts of death, hurting yourself, or suicide?
No, I haven't had any thoughts of hurting myself, death, or suicide. I don't want to end my life, I just feel very empty and completely lacking in any drive.

Have you noticed any changes in your self-confidence or how you feel about yourself as a person since these difficulties began?
I'm not really sure, and I haven't thought much about my self-confidence specifically. I've mostly just been feeling very flat, drained, and completely lacking my usual drive.
Have your husband, coworkers, or students noticed that you are moving or speaking more slowly than usual, or that you seem physically restless?

I haven't really noticed myself moving or speaking more slowly, nor have I felt physically restless. Nobody has mentioned those specific things to me, it's really just been the lack of drive and those moments where I completely lose my train of thought.
To help rule out other potential causes for these changes, do you have any known medical conditions, or have you recently started or changed any medications?

I don't have any major diagnosed medical conditions, although I did initially suspect some of this might just be general midlife changes. I am also not currently taking any medications, nor have I made any recent changes.
Do you regularly drink alcohol or use any recreational substances, and have you noticed any changes in your use of them over the past year?
I don't use any recreational drugs, and I only drink alcohol very occasionally, if at all. There hasn't been any change in my habits over the past year.
You mentioned suspecting these might be midlife changes. Have you experienced other symptoms like hot flashes, night sweats, or changes in your menstrual cycle?

No, I haven't really experienced those specific physical symptoms like hot flashes or night sweats. I think I initially just used "midlife concerns" as a vague explanation for my lack of energy and withdrawal because I didn't know how else to make sense of what was happening.
Have you also been experiencing significant anxiety, nervousness, or excessive worry since these changes began?

I haven't really been experiencing significant anxiety, nervousness, or excessive worry. Instead of feeling anxious, I mostly feel a profound lack of energy, drive, and interest. It feels more like I am empty and detached rather than nervous.
